# 0008: reuse a recent GC boundary check on latest-version reads

**What it changes.** Adds `src/sequenced_store.rs`. `ManifestStore` and `CompactionsStore` route their transactional reads and writes through `SequencedStore`, which skips the GC boundary re-read on a latest-version read when a full check inside the last window already proves the answer. The window is a fifth of the in-process garbage collector's `min_age` for that directory (60 s at the default 300 s). Writes, deletes and listings keep the full check. A database without boundary files or without an in-process collector skips nothing, and so do the admin, reader and standalone collector stores, which use the unchanged constructors.

**Why.** Each writer poll, compactor poll and worker poll re-reads `gc/<name>.boundary` after its probe. Stores bill that 304 or 404 as a full GET, so on an idle tablet the re-read was half of every poll's requests. Tests: `sequenced_store::tests` (7 tests).

**Why it cannot return data a full check would reject.** A full check at version `M` that started at `T` shows `M + 1` was missing at `T` and `M` was above the boundary. The collector advances the boundary only to a version that was not the latest when it listed and was older than `min_age`. Suppose a later read inside the window returns `N >= M`, after seeing `N + 1` missing, while the boundary is already at `V >= N`. If `V > M`, then `V`, and so `M + 1`, was created more than `min_age` before the read, which is before `T`; `M + 1` missing at `T` means it had been deleted, which needs the boundary at `M + 1` before `T`, contradicting the check at `T`. If `V = N = M`, then `M + 1` existed when the collector listed and is missing now, so it was deleted, which needs the boundary past `M + 1` and reduces to the first case. So the boundary at the probe is below `N`: the result is exactly what the unchanged read returns when its boundary GET is answered at the probe. The proof needs `window + clock skew + any backward step of the local clock + the longest a PUT stays invisible after its Last-Modified < min_age`; a fifth leaves 240 s at the default. A local clock behind the proof's start disables reuse.

**In-process collector.** `ManifestStore::advance_boundary` and `CompactionsStore::advance_boundary` go through `SequencedStore::advance`, which drops a proof at or below the new boundary once the advance is durable and before the collector deletes anything. Depot's only collector runs in the same process and shares the store, so for it the timing argument above is a second line of defense.

**Upstream.** Nothing equivalent; `slatedb-txn-obj` 0.17 always re-reads the boundary after its cached check passes. Candidate for an upstream option on `ObjectStoreBoundaryObject`.

**Drop when.** Upstream skips the re-read on its own, or Depot stops polling the manifest and `.compactions`.
